questions.q:
In an single visit, a 9-month old, unimmunized child can be given the following vaccination: 
a) Only BCG. 
 b) BCG, DPT-1, OPV-1. 
c) DPT-1, OPV-1, Measles. 
 d) BCG, DPT-1 OPV-1, Measles

Which of the following is low in human breast milk? 
a) Vitamin A 
 b) Vitamin C 
c) Vitamin K 
 d) Vitamin D

The route of Surfactant administration in hyaline membrane disease is:
a) Intravenous 
 b) Intramuscular 
 c) Inhalational 
 d) Intratracheal

Most common cause of osteomyelitis in sickle cell patients – 
a) Staphylococcus 
 b) Salmonella 
c) Streptococcus 
 d) H. Influenza

A 7 year old girl is able to draw shape of a Diamond, when asked to do so. Before she learnt drawing a diamond, she learned other shapes in the following sequence from 3 years to 7 years of age:
a) Circle – Rectangle – Square – Triangle
b) Square – Triangle – Rectangle – Circle
c) Rectangle – Triangle – Circle – Square
d) Circle – Square - Rectangle – Triangle

One of the vital steps in managing and preventing Meconium Aspiration Syndrome in a new born with meconium stained amniotic fluid is:
a) Noting APGAR when head is delivered
b) Applying suction in oral cavity and nasopharynx when head is delivered
c) Preventing hypothermia by reducing heat exposure.
d) Early Intubation in all cases, even with slight suspicion of MAS.

Earliest sign of pregnancy on an Obstetric ultrasound is:
a) Demonstration of an Embryo 
 b) Demonstration of Gestational Sac 
 c) Demonstration of Placental tissue
 d) None of the above

A newborn infant suffers from cyanotic heart disease caused by transposition of the great arteries (TGA). In this situation, the aorta arises from which of the following structures? 
a) Left atrium 
 b) Left ventricle
c) Right atrium. 
 d) Right ventricle

A premature female infant is born about 24 weeks after fertilization and develops rapid, labored breathing shortly after birth. She is immediately transferred to intensive care where she is diagnosed with hyaline membrane disease (HMD). Which of the following is most likely deficient in the infant? 
a) Alveolar ducts 
 b) Lung surfactant 
c) Terminal saccules 
 d) Type I alveolar cells

Which of the following pharmacological agent is used for the treatment of PDA? 
a) Indomethacin 
 b) Aspirin 
c) Prednisolone 
 d) PGI2

Vertical transmission rate of HIV infection from mother to baby is? 
a) 5 – 10% 
 b) 10 – 20%
c) 20 – 25% 
 d) 25 – 30%

An infant born to an elderly diabetic female shows signs of tachypnoea and cyanosis immediately after birth, infant’s arterial Oxygen saturation quickly worsens and he is shifted to cardiac cath lab to iatrogenically perforate the inter atrial septum where prostaglandin E1 was also infused. Hypoxia stabilizes and he is later shifted to definitve surgery what is the most likely diagnosis?
a) Patent Ductus arteriosus 
 b) Tetrology of fallot 
c) Transposition of great vessels 
 d) Tricuspid atresia.

All of the following are associated with elevate Alpha feto protein levels, except:
a) Down’s Syndrome 
 b) Meningomyelocele 
 c) Porter’s Syndrome 
 d) omphalocele

Anencephaly is the result of a defect in which of the following? 
a) Closure of the caudal neuropore 
 b) Closure of the rostral neuropore 
c) Formation of the first branchial arch 
 d) Formation of the somites

Floppy baby syndrome is seen in – 
a) Infant Botulism 
 b) RDS
c) Neonatal tetanus 
 d) Congenital rubella

The most common cause of meningitis in a one week old neonate is?
a) Infected maternal canal 
 b) Complicated Delivery
c) congenital rubella infection 
 d) Maternal meningitis

A 10 year old child presents with migratory joint pains involving knee, hip and elbow joints, fever, palpable subcutaneous nodules at posterior arm and elbow joint and a positive history of sore throat 1 month back, what is he most likely at risk for?
a) Aortic regurgitation 
b) Mitral Stenosis 
c) Aortic Stenosis 
 d) Mitral Regurgitation

Lymphocytic predominance and a normal glucose level on a CSF examination is suggestive of:
a) Bacterial meningitis 
 b) Viral meningitis
 c) Parasitic infection of CNS
 d) All of the above

Prenatally performed L:S ratio in a fetus is found to be 2.2. Which of the following statement is true about the fetus in postnatal life?
a) Fetus will not having cyanotic congenital heart disease
b) Fetus will not be having respiratory distress 
c) fetus will not have hydrocephalus
d) Fetus is not having Renal agenesis

Transient myeloproliferative disorder of the newborn is seen in association with: 
a) Turner syndrome. 
 b) Down syndrome. 
c) Neurofibromatosis. 
 d) Ataxia telangiectasia

The most appropriate drug used for chelation therapy in beta thalassemia major is: 
a) Oral desferrioxamine 
 b) Oral deferiprone
c) Intramuscular EDTA 
 d) Oral Succimer

All of the following vaccines are indicated in a 20 year old male suffering from Sickle cell disease, except? 
a) S. Pneumoniae 
b) S. Aureus 
c) H. Influenzae 
d) N. Meningitidis

A 14 year old girl is seen in pediatric clinic for progressive muscle weakness which increases as the day progresses, ptosis and blurring of vision. Which of the following conditions do not have a similar pathogenesis as present in this patient. 
a) Type I Diabetes Mellitus 
b) Rheumatoid arthritis 
c) Cushing’s Disease 
d) Grave’s Disease

A 3 day old infant is presented to you with viral meningitis and chorioretinitis, what is the drug of choice considering infection with a commonest virus: 
a) Gancicyclovir 
b) Amantidine 
c) Oseltamivir 
d) Ribavirin

Features of Nephrotic Syndrome include:
a) Oedema, Proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia
b) Oedema, Proteinuria and hyperalbunimemia
c) Oedema, Proteinuria and normoalbuminemia
d) None of the above

H. Influenzae type B vaccine will not impart protection against:
a) Pneumonia 
 b) Meningitis 
c) Otitis Media 
 d) None of the above

All of the following are features of Hirschprung’s disease except:
a) Constipation 
 b) Abdominal distention 
 c) Bleeding per rectum 
 d) Bilious vomiting

In prenatal diagnostic techniue Act 1994 which one of the following is not a ground for carrying out prenatal test ? 
a) Pregnant women above 35 years of age. 
b) History of two or more spontaneous abortion or fetal loss. 
c) When fetal heart rate is 160 per min at fifth and 120 per min at ninth month. 
d) History of exposure to potentially teratogenic drugs

Decreased Serum Albumin is predominantly seen in:
a) Vitamin A deficiency 
 b) Marasmus 
 c) Kwashiorkor 
 d) Scurvy

A new born is delivered via normal vaginal delivery, while attempting first breast feeding mother notices that the child suddenly turned blue and then normalized, what can be the most likely cause of this finding?
a) Tetralogy of Fallot 
 b) ASD 
 c) VSD 
 d) PDA

Most common cause of pneumonia in a infant 2 weeks of age is – 
a) Group B streptococcus 
 b) E coli 
c) Steroptococcus pneumoniae 
 d) Viral

Which vitamin deficient is most commonly seen in a pregnant mother who is on phenytion therepy for Epilesy?
a) Vitamin B6 
 b) Vitamin B12
c) Vitamin A. 
 d) Folic Acid

A ten day old premature neonate is found on routine investigations to have hypercalcemia. This is likely to be secondary to
a) phosphate depletion 
 b) excess intake of vitamin D
c) excess intake of milk 
 d) tertiary hyperparathyroidism

A mother is concerned because her one month boy has a swelling in his scrotum. He was born prematurely. On examination the swelling is seen to transilluminate. The likely cause is
a) Hydrocele 
 b) Testicular Torsion 
c) Epididymitis 
 d) seminoma

A 28 year old pregnant woman presents with red degeneration of fibroid. Management is - 
a) Myomectomy 
 b) Conservative
c) Hysterectomy 
 d) Termination of pregnancy

Hair on end appearance in skull X-ray is charac¬teristic of :
a) Spherocytosis 
 b) Sickle cell anemia
c) Thalassemia 
 d) Scurvy

The Vitamin A supplement administered in "Prevention of nutritional blindness in children programme" contain: 
a) 25,000 i.u./ml 
 b) 1 lakh i.u./ml 
c) 3 lakh i.u./ml 
 d) 5 lakh i.u./ml

All of the following are contraindications to Lumbar puncture except:
a) Papilledema 
 b) Unequal pupils 
 c) Suspected subarachnoid hemmorhage 
 d) Bradycardia

Which of the following vessels have highest oxygen concentration in a fetal circulation?
a) Umbilical Vein 
 b) Inferior Vena Cava 
 c) Umbilical Arteries 
 d) Ductus arteriosus

Swiss cheese appearance of endometrium on microscopy is characteristic of : 
a) Mucinous cystadenoma 
b) Metropathia hemorrhagica 
c) Endometriosis 
d) Endometrial carcinoma

Definitive treatment for foreign body aspiration in a child is:
a) history and physical examination
b) history and Heimlich maneuver
c) examination and chest X ray
d) History, examination and bronchoscopy

A newborn at birth manifests signs of intrauterine infections – microcephaly, congenital cataracts, Intrauterine growth retardation and hepatosplenomegaly. This condition could have been prevented with maternal administration of:
a) BCG Vaccine 
 b) MMR Vaccine 
 c) Intrapartum Ampicillin 
 d) Antenatal Iron & Folic Acid

A 9 year old boy is presented to you by his parents with complains of several episodes in a day where the child is unresponsive to verbal or tactile stimuli. He also has a history of progressive decline in scholastic performance. There is no history of fall or loss of memory following such episodes. Which of the following drug and it’s mechanism of action are most appropriate for the treatment of this child?
a) Phenytoin – decreases axonal conduction by blocking Na Influx
b) Ethosuximide – decreasing Ca influx through T type channels in thalamic neurons
c) Phenobarbitone – facilitation of Inhibitory GABA activity
d) Felbamate – Blocks NMDA receptors.

Drug of choice for nocturnal enuresis – 
a) Imipramine 
 b) Desmopressin 
c) Lamotrigine 
 d) Dobutamine

A 1 month old boy is referred for failure to thrive. On examination, he shows features of congestive failure. The femoral pulses are feeble as compared to branchial pulses. The most likely clinical diagnosis is :
a) Congenital aortic stenosis. 
 b) Coarctation of aorta.
c) Patent ductus arteriosus 
 d) Congenital aortoiliac disease.

All of the following are features of prematurity in a neonate, except:
a) No creases on sole. 
 b) Abundant lanugo.
c) Thick ear cartilage. 
 d) Empty scrotum.

The earliest immunoglobulin to be synthesized by the fetus is: 
a) IgA 
 b) IgG 
c) IgE 
 d) IgM

Treament of primary retinoblastoma is – 
a) Enucleation 
 b) Radiotherapy 
c) Chemotherapy 
 d) None of the above

Drug of choice for treatment for ADHD is – 
a) Methyphenidate 
 b) Amphetamine
c) Fluoxetine 
 d) Desimipramine

A 5 year old boy passed 18 loose stools in last 24 hours and vomited twice in last 4 hours. He is irritable but drinking fluids. The optimal therapy for this child is: 
a) Intravenous fluids 
 b) Oral rehydration therapy 
c) Intravenous fluid followed by oral fluids 
d) Plain water add libitum.
